# Jordan — Social

**Where things stand:** Jordan's social world right now is a small, load-bearing group: Mika, Dev, and until recently Lena at work. Mika is the constant — the friend who shows up uninvited with pad thai, who signs Jordan up for things before there's time to object, who has apparently refused for years to believe Jordan's "I'm fine." Dev is newer and still defining itself — musician, easy silences, now a real friendship that's survived Jordan testing it with a fake excuse and then walking that back. Lena left the company on 8/28 but hasn't left the picture; she's actively trying to pull Jordan out toward Northlight. The throughline across all of it: Jordan's pattern of work-stress triggering withdrawal, and specific people being the thing that ends it.

**How it got here:** It starts back on 7/31 with a run in Greenwood Park, where Mika makes the offhand observation that Coda (Jordan's side project) is the real portfolio, not a polished deck — an idea that recurs all summer. Through August, the pattern crystallizes and gets named explicitly (8/12, 8/24): work delivers a blow, Jordan shuts down and isolates, and eventually either drags himself to Groundwork or someone — almost always Mika — physically shows up (8/4 coffee-shop check-in, 8/24 pad thai on the floor). Dev enters via a nervous first walk at Greenwood Park on 8/8, which Mika had to talk Jordan out of cancelling. The friendship deepens fast: Coda comes up "almost by accident" and Dev gets genuinely invested, offering the idea that becomes the free-play feature. On 8/17 Mika strong-arms Jordan into an open mic, and the 8/21 performance of "Fast Car" at The Lantern becomes a real turning point — Dev and Mika meet, hit it off over obscure documentaries, and the three of them together feel, in Jordan's words, "easy and warm and like something I want to keep happening."

Then the reorg complicates things. On 8/24, bad news makes Jordan cancel on Dev with a fake excuse; on 8/27, Jordan chooses to tell Dev the truth instead, and Dev's response ("I disappear too, I just do it with a bass in my hands") lands as a real widening of the friendship — someone besides Mika now has permission to know when Jordan isn't fine. Lena's last day (8/28) removes Jordan's one office ally, but she pushes back hard against Jordan's reflexive self-doubt and promises to refer him at Northlight — a thread she picks up again on 9/1 when the actual reorg news lands (Jordan sidelined into "legacy marketing") and she texts "hang on."

The most recent entry, 9/3, is Dev finally using Coda for real — forty minutes of practice, eleven marked moments, all of them things going *wrong* rather than "highlights," which cracks open for Jordan how differently Dev practices (toward a gig, triage) versus how Jordan practices (toward feeling okay). It's a technical problem in the app, but it's also a small window into how the two of them are built differently as people, sitting in the same room, still finding it easy.

**Open threads:** Whether Lena's Northlight referral turns into anything real. Whether the Mika/Dev/Jordan three-way friendship keeps having nights like 8/21. Dev's gig on 9/19 — will Jordan go. Whether telling Dev the truth on 8/27 becomes the new default or was a one-time exception. And underneath it all, whether the "middle part" of the withdrawal cycle keeps shrinking on its own (as it did 9/1, twenty minutes instead of days) or whether that was a one-off.
